records.title: AGENT_GUIDE.md Recipes A, B, C crash immediately when run as written (3/3 tested, 3/3 broken)
records.evidence: Ran each snippet verbatim. Recipe A: `Covariate(t, stim, name='stim', xlabelval='time', xunitval='s', ylabelval='vel', yunitval='mm/s', dataLabels=['stim'])` raises `TypeError: Unexpected keyword arguments: xunitval, ylabelval, yunitval` — the real SignalObj/Covariate ctor only has `xlabelval, xunits, yunits` (no `xunitval`/`ylabelval`/`yunitval`). The built `cov` is also never passed into the following `Trial(nstc, ev=None, covarColl=None, neighbors=None)` call, which itself raises `TypeError: Trial.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ev'` (real kwargs are `events`/`event`, and there is no `neighbors` param at all). Recipe B: `TrialConfig(covariate_specs=[...], sampleRate=sample_rate, history_window_times=[...], ensCovHist=[])` — real `TrialConfig.__init__` signature is `(covMask=None, sampleRate=None, history=None, ensCovHist=None, ensCovMask=None, covLag=None, name='')`; `covariate_specs`/`history_window_times` don't exist. `Analysis.runAnalysisForAllNeurons(...)` doesn't exist either (real names are `RunAnalysisForAllNeurons` or `run_analysis_for_all_neurons`); and even with the real name, `fit = results[0][0]` raises `TypeError: 'FitResult' object is not subscriptable` — for this (1 neuron, 1 config) shape the correct unpack is `results[0]`. Recipe C: `Signal(t, rate_hz.reshape(-1,1), sampleRate=1000.0, dataLabels=['rate'])` raises `TypeError: Unexpected keyword arguments: sampleRate` (no such kwarg on Signal/SignalObj), and `simulate_poisson_from_rate(rate_signal, n_trials=5)` would also fail — real signature is `simulate_poisson_from_rate(time, rate_hz, rng=None)`, no `n_trials` parameter exists.
records.failure_scenario: A developer or an AI agent follows AGENT_GUIDE.md's own 'Recipe A/B/C' to build a Trial, fit a GLM, or simulate spikes, copy-pastes the exact code shown, and gets an immediate TypeError on the very first non-trivial line in all three cases — the opposite of what a 'toolbox usage guide' is for.
records.proposed_change:
Replace with verified-working code. Recipe A (drop unused `ev=None, neighbors=None`, fix Covariate kwargs, actually pass `cov`):
```python
import numpy as np
from nstat import Trial, Covariate, CovariateCollection, nspikeTrain, nstColl

sample_rate = 1000  # Hz
spike_times = np.array([0.012, 0.087, 0.123, 0.301])
st = nspikeTrain(spike_times, name="n1", sampleRate=sample_rate,
                 minTime=0.0, maxTime=1.0)

t = np.arange(0, 1.0, 1.0 / sample_rate)
stim = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 5 * t).reshape(-1, 1)
cov = Covariate(t, stim, name="stim", xlabelval="time", xunits="s",
                yunits="mm/s", dataLabels=["stim"])

nstc = nstColl([st]); nstc.setMinTime(0.0); nstc.setMaxTime(1.0)
covc = CovariateCollection([cov])
trial = Trial(nstc, covc)
```
Recipe B (fix TrialConfig kwargs, method name, result indexing — verified with Recipe A's `trial`):
```python
from nstat import TrialConfig, ConfigCollection, Analysis

cfg = TrialConfig(covMask=[["stim", "stim"]], sampleRate=sample_rate, name="stim_model")
configs = ConfigCollection([cfg])
results = Analysis.run_analysis_for_all_neurons(trial, configs)
fit = results[0]   # FitResult for neuron 0 under config 0 (1 config here)
print("AIC:", fit.AIC, "BIC:", fit.BIC)
print("KS stat:", fit.computeKSStats())
```
Recipe C (drop the nonexistent `Signal(... sampleRate=...)`/`n_trials=` usage; call the real 2-arg function):
```python
import numpy as np
from nstat import simulate_poisson_from_rate

t = np.arange(0, 5.0, 0.001)
rate_hz = 20 + 10 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * 1.5 * t)
spikes = simulate_poisson_from_rate(t, rate_hz, rng=np.random.default_rng(0))
```
Follow-up: Recipes D-H were not independently re-executed this pass; given 3/3 failed, add a CI gate that actually *executes* every AGENT_GUIDE.md python fence (not just import-checks it, see docs-11) so this class of drift is caught automatically.
records.verify_reason: Executed all three recipes verbatim with the installed nstat package and reproduced every claimed TypeError exactly: Covariate(... xunitval=, ylabelval=, yunitval=...) -> 'Unexpected keyword arguments: xunitval, ylabelval, yunitval'; Trial(nstc, ev=None, covarColl=None, neighbors=None) -> "got an unexpected keyword argument 'ev'"; TrialConfig(covariate_specs=..., history_window_times=...) -> "got an unexpected keyword argument 'covariate_specs'"; Signal(..., sampleRate=1000.0, ...) -> 'Unexpected keyword arguments: sampleRate'; simulate_poisson_from_rate(rate_signal, n_trials=5) -> "got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_trials'". Also confirmed FitResult has no __getitem__. Then ran the reviewer's full corrected_change for Recipe A+B end-to-end and it worked without modification, printing real AIC/BIC/KS values.

records.title: API reference is completely unlinked — root cause confirmed as docs/conf.py exclude_patterns, not a deploy-env/autodoc-import issue; fix verified
records.evidence: Built docs locally (clean checkout, package importable) and got the identical defect as the live site: every autosummary entry renders as `Name` with NO enclosing ``. A non-quiet build surfaces the real cause: `docs/api.rst:20: WARNING: autosummary: stub file not found 'nstat.SignalObj'. Check your autosummary_generate setting.` repeated for all ~56 entries — even though `docs/_autosummary/nstat.SignalObj.rst` etc. physically exist on disk (autosummary_generate=True did write them). `exclude_patterns = ["_build", "_autosummary", ...]` at conf.py:57 excludes that whole directory from Sphinx's known-document set, so the stub .rst files are never built into HTML and autosummary can't resolve a target to link to — hence a bare `` span. The conf.py comment (lines 73-76) rationalizes this as 'so the raw stubs aren't published — only the rendered HTML is', which is a misunderstanding: only `docs/_build/html` is ever deployed (confirmed in `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml`), never the `docs/` rst source tree, so excluding `_autosummary` from the source never protected anything and only broke the links. Fix verified: removed `"_autosummary"` from `exclude_patterns` in a scratch copy and rebuilt — stub warnings dropped from ~56 to 1 (an unrelated macOS-only case-collision, see docs-12), 71 `_autosummary/*.html` pages were generated, and `api.html` now renders ``. This also means the pack's 'likely env/autodoc-import' hypothesis is wrong — it reproduces with a plain local build of the current environment; deploy-docs.yml's `pip install -e .[dev]` step is not implicated.
records.failure_scenario: Every visitor to https://cajigaslab.github.io/nSTAT-python/api.html sees the full public API table (56+ symbols) but cannot click through to any per-symbol docstring page — defeating the page's stated purpose ('Click any symbol to jump to its rendered docstring').
records.proposed_change: In docs/conf.py:57, remove `"_autosummary"` from `exclude_patterns` (leaving `["_build", "Thumbs.db", ".DS_Store", "superpowers", "notebook_galleries", "parity"]`), and update/remove the now-incorrect rationale comment at conf.py:73-76. No change needed to `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml` — its warm-up+strict build steps already regenerate the stubs each run; once they're no longer excluded from the source set, the strict `-W` build should build and link them. Re-run `make docs-strict` locally to confirm 0 remaining 'stub file not found' warnings on this (Linux CI / case-sensitive) class of problem before merging, then redeploy via `gh workflow run deploy-docs.yml --ref main` per the repo's manual-deploy memory.
records.verify_reason: Root-cause diagnosis is correct and independently reproduced: a pre-existing docs/_build/html/api.html on disk already shows bare <code class="xref py py-obj docutils literal notranslate"> spans with no enclosing <a>, and removing '_autosummary' from docs/conf.py:57 exclude_patterns drops stub-not-found warnings from 72 to 1 and produces 130 working '_autosummary/*.html#...' links. BUT the 'fix verified'/apply-now framing is wrong: (1) the naive one-line fix introduces 119 NEW 'duplicate object description' warnings because every generated _autosummary/*.rst stub contains both '.. autoclass:: X' (which with napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True already documents __init__) AND an explicit '.. automethod:: __init__' directly below it. (2) Running the exact strict command the deploy pipeline uses, `python -m sphinx -W -b html docs ...`, exits 1 with this fix applied. (3) I additionally verified the CURRENT unmodified repo ALSO fails that same -W command today (exit 1) for unrelated reasons, so the strict build is already broken on main independent of this change.
records.verification_method: Built docs/_build/html already on disk (grep for xref span / href); rebuilt a scratch copy with /opt/anaconda3/bin/python3 -m sphinx -b html both with and without '_autosummary' excluded; ran -W on both the fixed and the as-committed docs tree and got exit 1 in both cases; diffed warning categories between builds, finding the new duplicate-object-description class only in the fixed build; inspected a generated stub .rst showing the duplicated autoclass+automethod directive.
records.corrected_change: Fixing exclude_patterns alone is necessary but not sufficient. Companion fix: resolve the autoclass/automethod duplication (set napoleon_include_init_with_doc = False, since the autosummary class template already emits an explicit '.. automethod:: __init__', or override that template) before removing '_autosummary' from exclude_patterns. Separately, the repo's -W strict build is already broken today; fix/triage that first. Verify by actually running `python -m sphinx -W -b html docs <scratch>` (not a non-strict build) and confirming exit 0 before merging.

records.proposed_change:
Add NumPy-style docstrings (one-liner + Parameters/Returns) to each of the 7 functions. Minimal example for fit_poisson_glm:
```python
def fit_poisson_glm(x, y, *, offset=None, include_intercept=True, l2=1e-6, max_iter=120, tol=1e-8) -> PoissonGLMResult:
    """Fit a Poisson GLM via damped Newton-Raphson with L2 ridge regularization.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : array_like, shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_features)
        Design matrix (or single covariate vector).
    y : array_like, shape (n_samples,)
        Observed (non-negative) counts.
    offset : array_like, optional
        Per-sample additive offset to the linear predictor (e.g. log exposure).
    include_intercept : bool, default True
        Prepend a constant column to ``x``.
    l2 : float, default 1e-6
        Ridge penalty applied to all non-intercept coefficients.
    max_iter : int, default 120
        Maximum Newton iterations.
    tol : float, default 1e-8
        Convergence tolerance on the L2 norm of the coefficient step.

    Returns
    -------
    PoissonGLMResult
    """
```
and similarly minimal docstrings for the other 6 (each is a short, self-contained function — a one-paragraph summary + Parameters/Returns suffices).

records.title: nspikeTrain's rendered class docstring omits the real sampleRate constructor parameter (drift between class docstring and __init__ docstring)
locations: nstat/_spike_train_impl.py:72-119 (__init__ docstring, NOT rendered by default)
records.evidence: `nspikeTrain.__init__` has a real positional parameter `sampleRate: float = 1000.0` (3rd positional arg). `__init__`'s own docstring documents it correctly and fully (lines 83-87: 'Sampling rate of the bin grid in Hz... Default 1000.0 Hz'). But the *class*-level docstring (lines 28-56) — the one Sphinx actually renders, since `docs/conf.py` never sets `autoclass_content` (default is `"class"`, i.e. only the class docstring, not `__init__`'s) — lists `spikeTimes, name, binwidth, minTime, maxTime, xlabelval, xunits, yunits, dataLabels, makePlots` and never mentions `sampleRate` at all. Verified against the actual built HTML (`docs_build_fixed/_autosummary/nstat.nspikeTrain.html`): the rendered 'Parameters' prose list has no `sampleRate` bullet (confirmed by extracting that exact `<dl class="field-list">` block), even though the page's auto-derived call signature shows `sampleRate=1000.0` with no explanation.
records.failure_scenario: A user reading the rendered API page for this frozen, MATLAB-parity-critical class sees `sampleRate=1000.0` in the signature but gets zero explanation of its meaning/units, and might miss that it even exists when skimming the prose Parameters list.
records.proposed_change: Add a `sampleRate` entry to the class-level docstring's Parameters list (copy the explanation already present in `__init__`'s docstring, lines 83-87), so the two docstrings agree. This same split pattern (class docstring maintained separately from a fuller `__init__` docstring) likely recurs elsewhere in `nstat/core.py` / `nstat/trial.py`; recommend a follow-up grep for `class \w+:\s*\n\s*"""` immediately followed later by a documented `def __init__` with its own `"""` to find other instances. (A broader, riskier alternative is setting `autoclass_content = "both"` in conf.py so both docstrings render — not recommended as the primary fix since it would duplicate prose for every other class.)
records.verify_reason: nstat/_spike_train_impl.py class docstring (lines 28-56) lists spikeTimes/name/binwidth/minTime/maxTime/xlabelval/xunits/yunits/dataLabels/makePlots and never mentions sampleRate, while __init__'s own docstring documents 'sampleRate : float, optional'. docs/conf.py has no autoclass_content setting, so Sphinx's default ('class') applies, meaning only the class docstring renders. records.title: Concrete fix for the snippet-checker's false positives: ast-based import extraction + skip inline-code-span links
records.evidence: Reproduced exactly the 5 false positives the evidence pack reported, with root causes traced to source: (1) AGENT_GUIDE.md:937,939,953 wrap literal markdown-syntax examples in backticks — `[text](path)`, `![alt](path)`, `[foo](file.md#section)` — but `_LINK_RE = re.compile(r"(!?)\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)")` matches `[...](...)`  anywhere in the raw text regardless of whether it's inside an inline code span, so these doc-about-the-checker examples get flagged as broken real links/images. (2) AGENT_GUIDE.md:306 `from nstat.analysis import Analysis  # GLMFitResult is also exported` — `_IMPORT_FROM_RE`'s `import\s+(.+)$` (MULTILINE, no DOTALL) captures the trailing `# ...` comment as part of the names blob, so `check_code_snippet_imports` tries to resolve the bogus name `"Analysis  # GLMFitResult is also exported"` and fails. (3) AGENT_GUIDE.md:374 `from nstat.extras.decoding import (` (multi-line parenthesized import) — the same regex's `(.+)$` stops at end-of-line and captures only `"("`, producing another bogus pseudo-name. Independently confirmed both underlying imports actually resolve cleanly when executed directly with Python.
records.failure_scenario: Because of these false positives, `check_readme_links.py` cannot currently be pointed at AGENT_GUIDE.md or docs/extras/*.md in CI (it would always report spurious failures), so those files have no automated snippet-staleness gate at all — exactly the gap that let AGENT_GUIDE.md's broken Recipes (docs-1) go undetected.
records.proposed_change: Two independent, composable fixes: (a) For links/images: before running `_LINK_RE.finditer`, strip inline code spans and fenced code blocks from a working copy of the text used only for link/image scanning (e.g. `re.sub(r'`[^`\n]+`', '', text)` plus the existing fence-stripping, or walk the markdown with a proper parser such as `markdown-it-py`/`mistune` and only visit `link`/`image` AST nodes — never raw-text regex over the whole document). This alone fixes all 3 of the AGENT_GUIDE.md link/image false positives, which are all backtick-quoted syntax examples. (b) For code-snippet imports: replace `_IMPORT_FROM_RE`/`_IMPORT_RE` regex scanning with `ast.parse(block_source)` and walk `ast.walk(tree)` for `ast.Import`/`ast.ImportFrom` nodes — `ast` natively handles multi-line parenthesized import lists, trailing `# comment`s, and `as` aliases correctly (each `alias.name`/`alias.asname` is already a clean token, no manual string splitting needed), and gracefully skips non-import statements in the same block. records.title: 3 of 4 isotropic edge-correction branches in spatial_gof.py recompute an r-independent per-pair weight inside the r_grid loop; the 4th (k_inhom) already does it correctly
records.evidence: In pair_correlation's isotropic branch, `fi = frac_disc_in_rect(pi_i[m], d[m], domain)` / `fj = frac_disc_in_rect(pi_j[m], d[m], domain)` depend only on the fixed pair distance d[m] and position, never on r/k, yet are recomputed inside `for k, r in enumerate(r_grid): ... for m in range(d.size): fi=...; fj=...`. In cross_k_inhom and cross_pair_correlation the same frac_disc_in_rect(point, d[i,j], domain) calls sit inside a per-r `for m in range(ii.size)` loop over the growing/kernel-windowed pair mask, so the same pair's weight is recomputed in every r-bin it participates in. By contrast k_inhom (lines 357-359) computes `fi`, `fj`, `w_iso` ONCE for all pairs before its `for k, r in enumerate(r_grid)` loop, which only does the masked sum -- proving the hoisted form is already the established, correct pattern in this file. Measured scaling of the unfixed pair_correlation(isotropic): n=150/300/300/600 points, 30/30/60/30 r-bins -> 0.0547s/0.2232s/0.3504s/0.8830s (n:150->300 at fixed bins=30 gives 4.08x, consistent with O(n^2); n:300->600 gives 3.96x).
records.proposed_change: Hoist the fi/fj/w_iso (or ker-masked weight) computation out of the r-loop in all 3 branches, mirroring k_inhom:355-364 exactly. Bit-identical: where the per-bin kernel/mask is 0 for a pair, old code already set that pair's contribution to 0 regardless of fi/fj; the new code computes the same finite fi/fj (floored at 1e-12 per frac_disc_in_rect's docstring) once and multiplies by the same 0 kernel/mask -> same 0 contribution. Leave the `border` branch (a different code path, not touched here) alone -- it carries a known pair-asymmetry numerics bug (separate memory item, Tier C, must not ride along in this vectorization PR.
records.verify_reason: The hoist IS bit-identical everywhere I tested it (np.array_equal True, max abs diff 0.0) -- confirmed by reimplementing pair_correlation's isotropic branch with fi/fj/w_iso hoisted outside the r-loop and comparing to the live nstat.extras.spatial.spatial_gof.pair_correlation at n=300, 30 bins. BUT the claimed performance benefit does NOT hold for pair_correlation / cross_pair_correlation: measured hoisted vs original at n=300/30-bins gave hoisted=0.259s vs original=0.224s, i.e. a 0.86x (14% SLOWER) hoist, not a speedup. Root cause: pair_correlation and cross_pair_correlation use a compact-support Epanechnikov KERNEL (`ker = epanechnikov((d-r)/bw)`), so each pair is only 'active' (ker!=0) in the handful of r-bins near r~=d[m] -- with r_grid spacing ~bw (the common case, confirmed in code at spatial_gof.py:203-204/822-823 where bw is clamped to the mean r_grid spacing), each pair is touched ~1-2 times either way, and hoisting instead FORCES fi/fj (frac_disc_in_rect, an O(1) but non-trivial geometric calc) to be computed for every pair including the many pairs with d[m] > max(r_grid)+bw that the current code never touches at all. By contrast, k_inhom/cross_k_inhom use a cumulative indicator `d<=r` (a growing mask, not a compact kernel) -- there every pair below a given r really is touched in every larger bin, so the hoist genuinely eliminates redundant work, exactly as k_inhom already demonstrates. The reviewer's own evidence (measurements_run) only timed the UNFIXED pair_correlation's overall n^2 scaling, never an isolated before/after of the hoist on that branch -- so the 'direct in-repo precedent, bit-identical' framing for all 3 branches is correct on correctness but wrong on the performance rationale for 2 of 3.
records.verification_method: Read spatial_gof.py:225-243 (pair_correlation isotropic, kernel-windowed), :355-364 (k_inhom isotropic, cumulative mask, already correct), :703-720 (cross_k_inhom isotropic, cumulative mask -- genuine analog of k_inhom), :843-859 (cross_pair_correlation isotropic, kernel-windowed, same issue as pair_correlation). If optimization is wanted there, first restrict the fi/fj computation to the pairs with d[m] within [0, max(r_grid)+bw] (a cheap prefilter), not to all O(n^2) pairs, and benchmark before/after at the actual n and bw this function is used with in production before claiming a win.
